chunks: 1. Al-Shaykh, may Allah have mercy on him, informed me from Abu al-Qasim Ja'far ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Ya'qub, from Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Safwan ibn Yahya, from 'Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Hajjaj, who said:

I asked Abu al-Hasan عليه السلام about a person with a fracture over which splints are placed, or who has a wound: how should he perform wudu (ablution), and at the time of ghusl (ritual bath) for janabah, and ghusl (ritual bath) of Friday? He said: He washes whatever the washing reaches of what is visible, of that over which there are no splints, and he leaves aside the rest of that which he is unable to wash. He does not remove the splints, and he does not tamper with his wound.
2. From him, from 'Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi 'Umayr, from Hammad, from al-Halabi, from Abu 'Abd Allah عليه السلام, that he was asked:

About a man who has an ulcer on his forearm or elsewhere in a place of wudu (ablution), so he binds it with a cloth, performs wudu (ablution), and wipes over it when he performs wudu (ablution). He said: If the water harms him, then let him wipe over the cloth; and if the water does not harm him, then let him remove the cloth and then wash it. He said: And I asked him about a wound—how should one deal with it in his ghusl (ritual bath)? He said: Wash what is around it.
3. Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Mahbub, from 'Ali ibn al-Hasan ibn Ribat, from 'Abd al-A'la, mawla of the family of Sam, who said: I said to Abu 'Abd Allah عليه السلام:
I stumbled and my nail broke off, so I placed a dressing upon my finger. How should I perform wudu (ablution)? He said: You know this and its like from the Book of Allah, Mighty and Majestic.
Allah, Exalted is He, said: “And He has not placed upon you in the religion any hardship.”
4. As for what Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya narrated, from Ahmad ibn al-Hasan, from 'Amr ibn Sa'id, from Musaddaq ibn Sadaqah, from 'Ammar, from Abu 'Abd Allah عليه السلام:

About a man whose nail breaks off: is it permissible for him to put gum upon it? He said: No. And he should not put upon it except what he is able to remove from it at the time of wudu (ablution), and he should not put upon it that to which water will not reach.

So the proper way to understand this report is that this is not permissible when one has a choice; but in a state of necessity, there is no problem with it, in accordance with what the first report contained.
5. As for what Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya narrated, from Ahmad ibn al-Hasan ibn 'Ali, from 'Amr ibn Sa'id, from Musaddaq ibn Sadaqah, from 'Ammar ibn Musa, from Abu 'Abd Allah عليه السلام:

Concerning a man whose forearm is broken, or a place from among the places of wudu (ablution), and he is unable to undo it due to the state of the setting when it has been set—how should he act? He said: When he wants to perform wudu (ablution), he should place a vessel containing water, and place the site of the setting in the water until the water reaches his skin; and that suffices him without undoing it.

So the proper way to understand this report is that we carry it upon a form of recommendation when that is possible and does not lead to harm. But if he fears harm from that, then nothing more is required than wiping over the splints, as we have explained.

key_terms.الِاسْتِحْبَابِ: recommendation rather than obligation in legal application
key_terms.الْجَبَائِرُ: splints or rigid dressings placed over a fracture or injury
key_terms.الْجِرَاحَةُ: a wound affecting the performance of ritual purification
key_terms.الْخِرْقَةِ: a cloth or bandage tied over an injured place
key_terms.الْمَسْحِ: wiping over a covering instead of direct washing
key_terms.الْوُضُوءِ: wudu (ablution), the ritual washing before salat (prayer)
key_terms.حَرَجٍ: hardship or constriction negated in the religion
key_terms.غُسْلِ الْجَنَابَةِ: ghusl (ritual bath) required after the state of janabah

ai.seo_question: How should a person perform wudu (ablution) or ghusl (ritual bath) when they have a wound, bandage, splint, or broken nail?
ai.summary: These reports set out the rulings for wudu (ablution) and ghusl (ritual bath) when a person has fractures, splints, bandages, wounds, or broken nails. The obligation is to wash whatever can be washed without harm, wipe over a covering when water is harmful, and avoid removing dressings or splints when that would cause hardship or injury. The cited Qur'anic principle, “And He has not placed upon you in the religion any hardship,” underlies this easing in ritual purity.
